lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are irrelevant personal details conventionally left off a résumé.

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant UX research experience.
items.because: With nearly six years of listed work, the degree is no longer the strongest introduction.

items.says: The page does not clarify your work situation since the last listed employment ended.
A 3:1 body-text contrast threshold does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.
items.because: Ordinary-sized text generally requires 4.5:1, and contrast alone cannot establish compliance for an entire design system.

items.says: The design-system work is not connected to the Senior UX Researcher role.
The line wrongly credits research synthesis itself with reducing repeat support calls.
items.because: The listed methods organize findings but do not change the customer experience or support workflow.

items.says: The 23% reduction is buried after the research counts and method list.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the most consequential result.

items.says: “Synthesizing” breaks the past-tense pattern in this ended role.
“Recommended fixes” does not identify what the shipped changes affected.
The three-of-five shipping result comes after the presentation detail.
“The number of tests run each quarter” is unnecessarily wordy.
The onboarding bullet opens with the assignment instead of the completed-sign-up increase.
items.because: Leading with the increase would show the value of the prototype testing on a quick scan.

items.says: The strongest Pinegrove result is not the entry’s opening bullet.
items.because: Readers encounter the card-dispute study before the stronger onboarding result.

items.says: The line incorrectly calls an average recommendation rating a Net Promoter Score.
items.because: Net Promoter Score subtracts the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters; averaging ratings produces a different measure.

items.says: The rating increase does not show what you contributed to it.
items.because: The line does not identify the research finding or recommendation behind the app change.

items.says: The calculation detail slows the rating bullet.
“The findings” does not name the insight behind the two-way reminder.
items.because: The line does not show what patients said that pointed toward two-way texting.

items.says: The drop in missed appointments is buried after the interview and reminder details.
items.because: A scanning reader sees the research activity before its measurable outcome.

items.says: The missed-appointments bullet should lead the Northwind entry.
items.because: It connects interviews, a product change and a measured reduction.

items.says: “Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in February 2022.
items.because: The date range and verb disagree.

items.says: The 30% reduction in support calls comes after the testing method.
items.because: A scanning reader sees the participant count before the outcome.

items.says: “The revised layout” does not identify the change prompted by testing.
The testing bullet says what was measured but not what the tests found.
“A 50% improvement” incorrectly describes the drop from 90 to 60 seconds.
items.because: The decrease is 30 seconds, or 33% of the original 90 seconds.

items.says: “By 20%” incorrectly labels a 20-percentage-point increase.
items.because: Moving from 65% to 85% adds 20 percentage points, while the relative increase is approximately 31%.

items.says: “Across 12 participants” repeats the participant count in the preceding bullet.
The audio-landmarks and color phrase repeats the methods in the preceding bullet.
The booking-flow bullet does not say what changed to remove five steps.
items.because: A reader cannot picture the design decision behind the before-and-after counts.

items.says: The drop in phone bookings has no stated comparison period.
items.because: “The next two months” gives the timing, not the baseline against which bookings fell.

items.says: The six resolved issues lack evidence of booking completion after the fixes.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether first-time users could then finish booking.

items.says: “Hallway testing” may be unclear to readers outside design teams.
The Methods skills line misspells “interviews.”
items.because: A spelling error in a UX research method can distract a reader.
